title: Implement ENTRYPOINT & CMD Patterns
description: Create a utility image using ENTRYPOINT and CMD, experimenting with overrides.
problemStatement:
## Objective
Deepen your understanding of ENTRYPOINT and CMD by building a `curl` utility image and testing different invocation patterns.

### Steps
1. Create a new directory and a `Dockerfile`:
   ```dockerfile
   FROM alpine:3.18
   RUN apk add --no-cache curl
   ENTRYPOINT ["curl"]
   CMD ["--help"]
   ```
2. Build the image as `curler:latest`:
   ```bash
   docker build -t curler .
   ```
3. Run the container without arguments:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm curler
   ```
   Expected: curl's help output.
4. Run with a URL:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm curler https://example.com
   ```
   Expected: HTML content of example.com.
5. Override CMD with different curl options:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm curler -v https://example.com
   ```
   Expected: verbose output from curl.
6. Override the ENTRYPOINT entirely to get a shell:
   ```bash
   docker run -it --entrypoint sh curler
   ```
   Inside the shell, verify curl exists. Type `exit`.
7. (Bonus) Modify the Dockerfile to have CMD as default options and ENTRYPOINT as `curl`. Then override CMD by passing a different URL and see that ENTRYPOINT remains.

### Deliverable
Provide the terminal commands and outputs from steps 3, 4, 5, and 6.
hints: If curl complains about missing CA certificates, add `apk add ca-certificates` or use `-k` for testing.
Remember that overriding CMD replaces all arguments, not appends.
expectedOutput: Step 3 shows curl help. Step 4 fetches example.com. Step 5 runs curl -v. Step 6 opens a shell.
solutionCode:
FROM alpine:3.18
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
ENTRYPOINT ["curl"]
CMD ["--help"]
# Build
docker build -t curler .
docker run --rm curler
docker run --rm curler https://example.com
docker run --rm curler -v https://example.com
docker run -it --entrypoint sh curler
